AI work-time survey and personal income: released hours need a paid-work channel

Five charts pair the Bank of Canada’s 2026 Q3 AI-work survey with independent paid-work and fixed-pay scenarios, keeping reported time, multiple-answer shares and cash receipts distinct.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Read the work-time survey, then enter an independent paid-work scenario

Interactive planning lab

Survey · additional hours estimated without AI, interpolated median4.7
Independent scenario · additional gross cash receipts$3,450
Independent scenario · cash change after tool cost, before personal tax$3,210

The first two panels reproduce published aggregate survey results from the Bank of Canada’s CSCE 2026 Q3 AI-work module, released 19 October 2026 and retrieved 25 October. Online collection was 5–27 August; follow-up interviews were 24 August–4 September. Hours are interpolated medians: active weekly use is estimated from reported duration categories and frequency, while additional time without AI is a respondent estimate of a counterfactual. The uses question permits multiple answers, so its shares overlap and need not sum to 100%. These are categorical observations, not a daily time series. No sample counts, response overlaps, causal productivity effect or earnings gain are inferred. The last three panels use independently entered weekly time, weeks, paid conversion, gross receipts per converted hour and out-of-pocket annual cost. They do not copy any survey median or response share into the scenario. All additional paid-work receipts are assumed actually received within this one-year horizon; no unpaid invoice or collection lag is added. A fixed-pay path assumes no overtime, bonus or pay rise and therefore has no extra receipts, but bears the same entered out-of-pocket cost. Cash change after that cost is before personal tax, other work costs and benefit changes; it is not take-home pay, business profit, a tax deduction or proof of affordability. No monetary value is imputed to leisure, quality, learning or the person’s existing salary.

The central idea

Time released from a task can improve quality, learning or life outside work. Additional household cash requires a separate compensation arrangement and actual receipts after relevant costs.

01

Read the work-time observation before turning it into money

The Bank of Canada's 2026 Q3 Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations included questions about AI use at work, time required for tasks and uses of the time respondents felt they had released. Those answers provide context about workers' reported experiences.

The report was released on 19 October 2026. Online responses were collected from 5 to 27 August, and follow-up interviews ran from 24 August to 4 September. The reference quarter, collection period and release date are different pieces of information.

The two survey charts are categorical summaries from that release. They are not a daily series, a record of each respondent's working hours or an experiment assigning people randomly to use AI. The article does not infer an effect on wages, paid working time or household income from those summaries.

The separate calculator begins with independently chosen weekly time and compensation assumptions. It does not turn an aggregate survey median into a personal prediction or transfer a reported time-use percentage into a revenue conversion rate.

02

The two hour measures have different definitions

The first source panel reports 2.8 hours per week for active AI use and 4.7 hours for additional time respondents estimated they would need to complete their tasks without AI. Both retain the source's interpolated-median label.

Active weekly time is estimated from each respondent's reported duration category and frequency of use. The source uses category midpoints and assigns 7.5 hours to the open-ended daily category above six hours. The aggregate therefore depends on an explicit estimation method rather than a time-clock record.

The other measure asks about additional work time in a hypothetical week without access to AI. It is a respondent counterfactual estimate. It does not become a directly observed causal productivity gain merely because it is summarized numerically.

Subtracting the active-use median from the additional-time median would not establish an individual's net saving. The questions describe different roles, and the difference of aggregate medians is not automatically the median of individual differences. Likewise, multiplying 4.7 by an assumed wage would introduce compensation assumptions absent from the survey.

03

Time-use shares overlap and do not allocate a single pie

The second source panel asks respondents to select every applicable use of the time they felt AI had helped release. The listed options concern task quality, additional tasks, work-life balance, learning or training, and creative work.

Because more than one answer is allowed, these percentages are not mutually exclusive groups. The five displayed shares sum to 209.20%, which is compatible with a multiple-response question. Renormalizing them to 100% would answer a different question and hide that design.

The percentages retain the denominator of respondents to this saved-time question in the AI-work module. They are not percentages of all Canadians, shares of the working week or the probability that a particular worker will receive additional pay.

The aggregate extract does not identify response overlaps or how many hours were assigned to each use. Reporting additional tasks also does not establish additional compensation. A fixed-pay employee can complete more work while receiving the same salary.

04

Enter a separate route from usable time to actual receipts

The default scenario independently assumes three usable hours released per week across forty-six weeks. That creates 138 hours of potential capacity. It is deliberately separate from the survey's 4.7-hour estimate.

The reader then assumes 50% of that capacity becomes additional paid work, producing sixty-nine paid hours. At CAD 50 of additional gross cash received per converted hour, those hours generate CAD 3,450 of extra receipts during the modeled year.

The annual out-of-pocket tool cost is independently set to CAD 240. The waterfall deducts that cost once, leaving CAD 3,210 of cash change before personal tax and other work costs. It is not after-tax take-home pay, business profit or an automatic tax deduction.

Every link is a separate assumption: capacity must be usable, additional work must exist, someone must agree to pay for it and cash must actually arrive within the horizon. An unpaid invoice is not counted as a receipt. The example makes no claim about a market hourly rate, demand or the probability of achieving the selected conversion.

05

A fixed salary can leave cash unchanged while time has value

The comparison path assumes the same out-of-pocket tool cost but no overtime, bonus or salary increase. Additional receipts are therefore zero, and the narrow cash change is negative CAD 240 at the defaults.

This does not mean released time has no value. It may improve quality, reduce pressure, support training or leave more time outside work. Those benefits are simply not priced as additional income in this cash calculation.

If an employer pays the tool cost, enter zero personal out-of-pocket cost for the relevant comparison. If compensation changes through an actual agreement, use the confirmed receipt amount and timing. Do not assume that an employee automatically receives an hourly payment for every hour a task takes less time.

The paid-work and fixed-pay bars compare defined arrangements. A negative result means the entered cost exceeds additional receipts in that narrow scenario, rather than that the person's total household earnings are negative. Existing salary, ordinary expenses and taxes are outside the chart.

06

Test conversion and cost before adding the result to a budget

The matrix varies paid conversion and annual out-of-pocket cost while retaining the independently chosen weekly time, weeks and gross receipts per converted hour. A zero-conversion row makes the cost visible even when no extra paid work materializes.

The official survey panels remain fixed when those controls change. An editable scenario is not a revision to the published evidence, and a favorable scenario cell does not establish that the worker can achieve it.

Before including extra cash in a personal plan, confirm the work arrangement, actual compensation, collection timing and associated expenses. Determine the relevant personal-tax and benefit effects separately. A pre-tax cash comparison alone does not tell the household how much can safely be spent or saved.

The five charts connect the questions without collapsing them: reported hours, overlapping uses of time, a paid-receipt bridge, two compensation arrangements and a conversion/cost matrix. Keep evidence about tasks separate from the contractual and cash conditions that turn a change in work into a change in household resources.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. The first two panels reproduce published aggregate CSCE AI-work results for 2026 Q3. The last three are independently authored hypothetical cash scenarios. No causal time-saving effect, earnings increase or AI product return is inferred from the survey. Original scenario calculations and research checklists are TickerLantern’s educational analysis; attributed publisher examples retain their stated source and scope. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.

  1. Bank of Canada · CSCE 2026 Q3, Box 1 ↗

    Released 19 October 2026; retrieved 25 October 2026. Governing questions, interpolated-median method and multiple-answer context. No interview quotation, causal inference or source estimate of additional earnings is reproduced.

  2. Bank of Canada Valet · AI-work hours, chart 1-A ↗

    Retrieved 25 October 2026. Two categorical hour observations with the estimation note retained. The actual Category dimension governs interpretation; the API date-format hint does not turn category keys into daily dates.

  3. Bank of Canada Valet · Uses of time, chart 1-B ↗

    Retrieved 25 October 2026. Five category shares in published percent units. Multiple selections are retained without normalizing to a pie, estimating response intersections or converting shares into hours.
